title: Prescriptions Handling Class Schedule: Validity Periods and Refill Caps
content:
Every prescription held under Kestrel Prescriptions sits in one handling class, and the class fixes two limits for the life of the record: how long the prescription can be filled, and the highest number of refills Kestrel records on it.

## Schedule

| Handling class | Validity period (calendar days from the written date) | Highest number of refills recorded |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Controlled Acute Prescription | 365 | 11 |
| Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription | 365 | 11 |
| Schedule V Controlled Prescription | 365 | 11 |
| Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription | 180 | 5 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | 90 | 0 |
| Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription | 365 | 11 |

## Terms of the schedule

1. **Validity period.** The validity period is counted in calendar days from the date the prescriber wrote the prescription, the written date being day 0. The prescription can be filled during that period.
2. **Refill cap.** The refill cap is the highest number of refills Kestrel records on a prescription of the class. Refills written above the cap are recorded at the cap.

## Reading the schedule (hypothetical figures)

- A Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription written on a given date, day 0, has a validity period of 180 calendar days; the 180th calendar day after the written date is still inside the period.
- A Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription on which the prescriber wrote 8 refills is recorded with 5 refills, the cap for that class.
- A Schedule II Controlled Prescription is recorded with 0 refills whatever number of refills is written on it, and its validity period is 90 calendar days.
- A Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription written with 3 refills is recorded with 3 refills, which is under the cap of 11.
